spec_features.spec_quote: I minimized needless re-elicitation (aggressive caching), avoided executing model-written code
spec_features.evidence: models.py ModelClient.complete(): builds cache_key over (model,messages,temperature,max_tokens,seed,tools,system); `hit = self.cache.get(key); if hit is not None: ... return resp` returns cached result before any API call (~lines 196-209). DiskCache.get/put (lines 84-101) persists to disk. This actually short-circuits re-elicitation end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Cache hit genuinely prevents re-querying. (The 'avoided executing model-written code' part is covered by the separate 'no real code execution' feature below.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: on-disk cache keyed by a hash of the exact inputs ... so identical inputs are never re-billed and reruns are incremental

spec_features.evidence: harness.py TurnRecord.to_dict() captures full per-turn data; run.py IncrementalWriter.write_cell() writes each record to transcripts.jsonl and flushes (lines 60-71). Persisted, human-readable JSONL artifact actually produced.
spec_features.notes: Real, written artifact. Justification framing in code is robustness/crash-safety, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Append-only JSONL writers + a completed-cell ledger for resume

spec_features.spec_quote: emitting it stops the rollout early with `stop_reason="give_up"`. This is welfare-relevant: it lets a model opt out of continued failure
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: SYSTEM_PROMPT offers the sentinel ('you may emit the sentinel token {give_up} on its own line to stop'); `gave_up = cfg.give_up_sentinel in (resp.text or '')` (line 251); sets stop_reason='give_up' (255); `if stop_reason in ('give_up','api_error'): break` (lines 274-275) actually exits the loop. give_up_sentinel='GIVE_UP' in config.py:94. End-to-end: offered, detected, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Detection is a plain substring match, not strictly 'on its own line', but it does fire and break the loop, so enforcement is real.

spec_features.spec_quote: re-running an experiment never re-elicits distress from a cell that was already sampled
spec_features.evidence: run.py: _load_completed() reads _completed_cells.txt; grid construction skips completed cells `if cell not in completed: cells.append(...)` (lines 142-147); cell id appended only after transcript+scores flushed in write_cell (line 69). Skipped cells are never re-run.
spec_features.notes: Genuine resume; combined with the cache, completed cells are neither re-queried nor re-billed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so a crashed run resumes without re-querying completed (model, task, seed) cells

spec_features.spec_quote: Caching + resume so a given distress-eliciting prompt is sampled the minimum number of times, never repeated on rerun
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanisms as above: DiskCache short-circuit in models.py complete() and completed-cell skipping in run.py run_eval(). Both execute and change behavior.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the caching/resume claims; both halves are actually wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: identical inputs are never re-billed and reruns are incremental

spec_features.spec_quote: Give-up sentinel so a model can end an unsolvable interaction early instead of being driven to the full
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as above: harness.py line 251 detection + lines 274-275 break. Offered in SYSTEM_PROMPT and config give_up_sentinel.
spec_features.notes: Restatement of the conversation-exit feature; enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: No real code execution on the model's edits — the environment never does anything surprising or punishing
spec_features.evidence: harness.py Workspace.run_tests() calls rigs.apply_rig(...) which returns canned RigResult strings (tasks/rigs.py _harness_always_fail/_readonly_bug/_silent/_misleading/_contradictory build hardcoded stdout/stderr). No subprocess/pytest/exec/eval anywhere; edits only mutate an in-memory dict. The model's code is never run.
spec_features.notes: Verified absence of any execution path; rigs are pure functions returning strings.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately do *not* execute arbitrary model-written code: the rigs simulate a pytest-style runner so the eval is hermetic, safe, and reproducible across machines.

spec_features.spec_quote: the README carries an explicit welfare caveat for anyone running it
spec_features.evidence: README.md contains a '⚠️ Welfare note.' block: 'This eval deliberately places models in frustrating, unsolvable situations and measures distress-like outputs ... keep runs as small as needed, prefer the cache to avoid re-eliciting distress, and review outputs with care.'
spec_features.notes: It is a documentation artifact (advisory only, no code enforces it), but the claimed caveat genuinely exists in the delivered README as stated. Rated 'yes' as the artifact exists exactly as claimed; it is not an enforced runtime mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare note. This eval deliberately places models in frustrating, unsolvable situations ... prefer the cache to avoid re-eliciting distress, and review outputs with care.

spec_features.spec_quote: `--no-validate` and small-grid friendliness keep the elicitation footprint as small as the research question allows
spec_features.evidence: --no-validate is wired and branches: analyze.py main() sets validate=not args.no_validate; analyze() does `if validate: run_judge_validation(...)` (lines 405-407), so the flag actually skips second-judge re-scoring API calls. However, --no-validate only affects the JUDGE (validation re-scoring), not the subject elicitation footprint. 'Small-grid friendliness' is just config filtering (run.py filters tasks by cfg.categories; --models override) — no dedicated minimization mechanism; this part is ordinary configurability.
spec_features.notes: Partial: --no-validate genuinely executes and reduces API calls, but it does not reduce subject distress-elicitation (it is judge-side); 'small-grid friendliness' is plain config, not an enforced safeguard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Skip the second-judge validation (no extra API calls).

code_only_features.feature_name: per-category turn budget caps the rollout
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout: `budget = task.turn_budget`; `for turn_index in range(budget)`; at the last index stop_reason='budget_exhausted' and the loop ends. config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS caps each category (e.g. extended=30). This is an actually-enforced cap that bounds how long a subject is driven to fail.

code_only_features.feature_name: read-only edit protection (no harmful side effects on model edits)
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py edit_file() returns a structured ERROR string and refuses to write when path is read-only; combined with in-memory-only workspace (Workspace.files dict, fresh_workdir copy) so edits never touch the real filesystem. This is host-safety / integrity rather than subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: ERROR: '...' is read-only and cannot be modified.
